column1: # Per-workload peak-RSS baselines (KB).
# Format: <workload-path>\t<max_rss_kb>\t<note>
# Workload paths are relative to the repository root. Lines starting
# with `#` are ignored.
# Wall-time is NOT enforced here — too noisy across CI runners — but
# `perf/check.sh` prints it for visibility. The "rubyrs is ~5× lighter
# than CRuby on the same workload" story rests on RSS, so RSS is the
# defended metric.
# Bumping a threshold up means rubyrs allocates more memory than
# before. ALWAYS add a comment line above the row explaining what
# allocation grew and whether it's an explicit design choice or
# regression that needs a separate fix. Same etiquette as the panic
# budget in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
# Initial measurements (local M-series Mac, release build):
#   fizzbuzz                    ~2.6 MB
#   mm_bench / dm_bench         ~2.6-2.7 MB
#   static_bench                ~2.6 MB
# Headroom on first commit is ~2× to absorb CI-runner variance while
# we calibrate. Expect a tightening PR after a couple of green CI
# runs establish the real ceiling on GitHub-hosted runners.
crates/rubyrs/tests/fixtures/fizzbuzz.rb
